reading.body:
The American Bankers Association is the client on 12 AI lobbying filings, and 32 lobbyists are named across them.

The filings cluster tightly. Twenty of the 32 lobbyists appear on 11 or 12 filings each, which means the same group of people is named on nearly every report. This is not a broad, rotating roster. It is a standing team that files repeatedly on AI, with a smaller tail of lobbyists appearing on 2 to 8 filings.

The data covers who filed and who was named. It does not cover what position the ABA argued, what the AI bills said, or whether the lobbying changed any outcome. A filing reports that a client lobbied on an issue, not the stance taken. The counts also do not distinguish between filings on separate bills and repeated filings on the same bill.

Nothing here connects to compute, buildings, or power. Banking trade lobbying on AI is about financial regulation, not data center siting or electricity supply, and the data gives no basis for linking the two.

summary: AMERICAN BANKERS ASSOCIATION filed 12 Lobbying Disclosure Act reports on AI held by this site. Its clients, the lobbyists named on those filings and the AI bills they name are below. LDA registrant id 1785.
